title: 2021 AMC 12A Problem 16
statement:
In the following list of numbers, the integer \(n\) appears \(n\) times in the list for \(1 \le n \le 200.\) \(1,\) \(2,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(3,\) \(3,\) \(4,\) \(4,\) \(4,\) \(4,\) \(\ldots,\) \(200,\) \(200,\) \(\ldots,\) \(200\)

What is the median of the numbers in this list?

solutions.text:
The list has \(1 + 2 + \cdots + 200\) \(= \dfrac{200\cdot 201}{2}\) \(= 20100\) terms, so the median is the average of the \(10050\)th and \(10051\)st terms.

The value \(n\) occupies positions up to \(\dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}.\) Since \(\dfrac{141\cdot 142}{2} = 10011\) and \(\dfrac{142\cdot 143}{2} = 10153,\) positions \(10012\) through \(10153\) all equal \(142.\) Both middle positions fall in this block, so the median is \(142.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
